headline: PAGASA Tracks LPA East of Northern Luzon as Habagat Keeps Parts of Luzon, Western Visayas Wet
seoTitle: PAGASA Tracks LPA East of Northern Luzon | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA spotted an LPA about 1,030 km east of Northern Luzon while the southwest monsoon continued to bring rain and rougher seas to parts of Luzon and western Visayas.
deck: The low-pressure area was about 1,030 kilometers east of Northern Luzon early Thursday, while the southwest monsoon continued to affect Luzon and the western Visayas.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: PAGASA was monitoring a low-pressure area about 1,030 kilometers east of Northern Luzon at 3 a.m. Thursday, while the southwest monsoon continued to affect Luzon and the western section of the Visayas.

Zambales and Occidental Mindoro were forecast to experience occasional rains, while Metro Manila, the Ilocos Region, Cordillera Administrative Region, the rest of Central Luzon, Batanes, parts of Calabarzon, Palawan and several Western Visayas provinces were forecast to have scattered rains and thunderstorms.

sections.heading: Risks and sea conditions
paragraphs: PAGASA warned that moderate to heavy rain and severe thunderstorms could trigger flash floods or landslides in susceptible areas.
Moderate to strong southwesterly winds were forecast over Luzon and the western Visayas, with moderate to rough coastal waters and waves of about 1.5 to 3.4 meters.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: An LPA is a developing area of relatively low atmospheric pressure and is not automatically a tropical cyclone. Its position and organization can change between forecast cycles, while the southwest monsoon can produce hazardous rain and seas independently of whether the disturbance becomes a named storm.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Communities already saturated by recent monsoon rains remain vulnerable even when rainfall becomes intermittent. Travelers, fishers and residents near slopes and waterways should use current local warnings rather than rely only on the LPA's distance from land.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: PAGASA will continue monitoring the LPA and the southwest monsoon. Forecasts can change quickly, so rainfall, thunderstorm and marine advisories should be checked against the latest official bulletin before travel or outdoor activity.
